purpose: Complete the hostile, oceanic, transport, Nether and End resource integration layer so production remains complete while reading as believable local industry inside each civilization.
rules_carried_forward: Visible farm architecture belongs to the local civilization even when internal machinery is standardized.
Primary processing stays near the ecosystem that feeds it unless a downstream process has a stronger cultural/economic home elsewhere.
Dangerous farms justify stronger physical separation, containment and restricted circulation.
The Grand Exchange redistributes; it does not absorb source-region processing.
Transit Isles moves people and cargo; it does not become a generic manufacturing region.
All wood/tree families, including Nether wood families, remain consolidated under the Timberlands Wood & Tree system. Ember Coast handles non-wood Nether vegetation and Nether-native production only.
Bone meal remains part of the Agriculture ecosystem. Haunted Marches exports bones; Breadbasket owns conversion and fertilizer integration.
Every major production district needs visible inputs, outputs, storage, maintenance access and a believable connection to local housing/civic life.

Overworld Hostile Mob.why_here: A fortified frontier culture already organizes daily life around controlled danger, watchkeeping and containment, making hostile-mob production a civic survival industry rather than an arbitrary farm district.
Overworld Hostile Mob.farm_architecture: Wall-ring mobworks, blast-separated powder magazines, catacomb bone galleries, fletcher yards, ravine webworks, elevated watch paths and sealed service corridors.
Overworld Hostile Mob.settlement_expression: The capital coordinates mixed hostile output, while creeper, skeleton and spider systems occupy specialized satellite settlements with different containment logic. Ruins and funerary sites keep the region from reading as one industrial perimeter.
local_processing: bones stored for export rather than centrally converted to bone meal
imports: Engineer's Reach redstone and safety controls
trade_routes: secure freight to Transit Isles rocket works
string/slime component trade through Grand Exchange
Overworld Hostile Mob.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Bones move to Breadbasket fertilizer works; gunpowder moves primarily to Transit rocket production and specialty uses; string feeds utility/craft systems. Dangerous overflow is stored in detached magazines, not ordinary warehouses.
Overworld Hostile Mob.player_build_guidance: Let defenses, inspection points and restricted service roads make the mechanics believable. The player should feel that the settlements grew around managing danger.

Fishing / Kelp / Drowned / Tidal Process.why_here: A civilization rebuilt around tides, lagoons and drowned ruins naturally treats the sea as farmland, road and industrial power source at once.
Fishing / Kelp / Drowned / Tidal Process.farm_architecture: Low stilt villages, fish houses, net lofts, kelp racks, submerged cultivation fields, drowned-control channels, tidal gates, water wheels, salvage quays and storm refuges.
Fishing / Kelp / Drowned / Tidal Process.settlement_expression: Ordinary fishing villages remain dense and domestic; kelp farming visibly extends into the sea; drowned systems are fortified and separated by controlled channels; tidal processing becomes civic infrastructure rather than a hidden machine room.
local_processing: tidal-powered or water-themed processing where appropriate
trade_routes: Blue Pilgrimage/merchant lane to Sapphire Coast
Fishing / Kelp / Drowned / Tidal Process.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Kelp supports fuel and processing chains; fish supplies Hearthlands; drowned copper and specialty drops feed craft/engineering markets; salvage creates repair stock for coastal settlements.
Fishing / Kelp / Drowned / Tidal Process.player_build_guidance: Make water levels, current direction, gates and piers legible. Production should look impossible to separate from the tide.

Amethyst & Sculk / Dripstone.why_here: The civilization formed around geodes, ancient geometry and deep-cave research, so amethyst, sculk and dripstone production become scholarly/extractive institutions instead of surface-style mines.
Amethyst & Sculk / Dripstone.farm_architecture: Geode galleries, resonance halls, sealed sculk laboratories, sensor bridges, dripstone collection basins, rock archives, lift stations and controlled cavern walkways.
Amethyst & Sculk / Dripstone.settlement_expression: Amethyst works remain bright and public-facing; sculk production is restricted and quiet; dripstone geology is practical and research-oriented; the capital and transit caverns bind them together without making one continuous underground factory.
trade_routes: restricted research exchange with Shrouded Isles
Amethyst & Sculk / Dripstone.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Amethyst supports decorative and technical builds; dripstone directly supports Volcano lava systems; sculk remains controlled high-risk cargo with limited storage destinations.
Amethyst & Sculk / Dripstone.player_build_guidance: Do not make cave farms look like surface warehouses. Preserve void, darkness, acoustics and long bridge approaches as part of the industrial design.

Ocean & Guardian / Coral / Prismarine.why_here: A reef-city civilization already treats underwater and shoreline space as one continuous urban realm, making guardian production, coral stewardship and prismarine craft culturally central.
Ocean & Guardian / Coral / Prismarine.farm_architecture: Monument districts, submerged service galleries, pale sea towers, prismarine yards, reef gardens, ceremonial water gates and channel-control structures.
Ocean & Guardian / Coral / Prismarine.settlement_expression: Guardian production is monumental and heavily engineered; coral production/stewardship is ecological and low-density; prismarine craft and navigation become prestigious civic industries.
local_processing: coral stewardship and decorative marine material handling
trade_routes: Blue-water merchant lane to Grand Exchange
Southern sea road to Isles of Plenty
Ocean & Guardian / Coral / Prismarine.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Prismarine becomes a visible prestige export in ports and marine institutions; guardian lighting resources support monumental civic lighting; coral remains stewardship-heavy rather than bulk extraction imagery.
Ocean & Guardian / Coral / Prismarine.player_build_guidance: The farm should visually read as part monument, part city utility. Underwater access and shoreline public space should be designed together.

Rocket & Transportation.why_here: The neutral crossroads civilization exists to standardize movement, transfer and route law across otherwise independent cultures.
Rocket & Transportation.farm_architecture: Grand terminals, rail halls, switching towers, freight yards, ferry halls, rocket/firework works, landing terraces, lighthouse stations and route-control forts.
Rocket & Transportation.settlement_expression: Rail, maritime, freight, traveler-service, route-control and flight functions occupy different islands. Shared signs, platform geometry and transfer logic unify them despite borrowed architectural materials.
local_processing: rocket/firework autocrafting from imported gunpowder and paper
imports: Blackfen/Isles of Plenty paper or sugar-cane-derived inputs
trade_routes: guarded Nether and End transfer routes
Rocket & Transportation.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Transit consumes rather than owns many resources. Empty containers, return freight and maintenance parts should visibly circulate back to source regions.
Rocket & Transportation.player_build_guidance: Make transfers visible. A player should be able to see where cargo changes from ship to rail, rail to portal freight, or local transport to long-distance flight.

Nether Vegetation (non-wood).why_here: Portal administration and controlled Nether horticulture belong near the safest permanent gateway infrastructure.
Nether Vegetation (non-wood).farm_architecture: Fortified greenhouse courts, nether-wart terraces, fungi gardens, protected soul-soil plots and quarantine-style storage rooms inside the portal capital.
Nether Vegetation (non-wood).settlement_expression: Vegetation districts provide a rare cultivated counterpoint to the blackstone fortress city. They are enclosed, carefully regulated and visually separated from civic portal courts.
local_processing: Nether wart and non-wood vegetation collection
exports: Nether wart and other non-wood Nether vegetation
trade_routes: guarded portal freight to Transit Isles
Nether Vegetation (non-wood).byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Crimson/warped wood output is explicitly excluded from this ecosystem and remains in the Timberlands Wood & Tree system.
Nether Vegetation (non-wood).player_build_guidance: Use horticultural courts and controlled plots, not generic farm rows. The point is that cultivation inside a hostile dimension required institutional protection.

Gold & Piglin.why_here: The Piglin exchange district grew around access to Nether gold and controlled barter, creating a mercantile-fortified economy distinct from ordinary surface trade.
Gold & Piglin.farm_architecture: Gold works, barter galleries, fortified exchange courts, secure vaults, sorting halls and guarded loading chambers.
Gold & Piglin.settlement_expression: The district feels like a citadel-market: dense, valuable and heavily controlled, with clear separation between public exchange, dangerous production and secure storage.
Gold & Piglin.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Barter outputs split onward toward brewing, building, End expeditions and technical systems instead of remaining centralized here.
Gold & Piglin.player_build_guidance: Use visible security and value handling. Gold should influence the district's architecture without turning every surface into gold blocks.

Blaze & Wither.why_here: Fortress-derived hostile production requires the strongest containment culture in Ember Coast and is deliberately segregated from the Piglin/gold district on the same island.
Blaze & Wither.farm_architecture: Fortress-spire compounds, sealed blaze galleries, wither containment yards, blast-resistant service tunnels and remote maintenance towers.
Blaze & Wither.settlement_expression: This district is austere, sparse and restricted, with buffer zones separating it from gold/barter neighborhoods.
trade_routes: End expedition supply route through Shrouded access
Blaze & Wither.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Blaze output supports brewing and End progression systems; dangerous wither-related goods use bonded storage rather than ordinary warehouses.
Blaze & Wither.player_build_guidance: Make buffer distance and containment part of the skyline. This should be the least domestically integrated district on Island_126.

Ghast / Magma / Froglight.why_here: Open ash-coast terrain and separated causeways allow large hostile systems and frog-linked froglight production to coexist without overrunning inhabited districts.
Ghast / Magma / Froglight.farm_architecture: Tall ghast-control structures, magma works, froglight towers, protected frog transfer chambers and heat-resistant service causeways.
Ghast / Magma / Froglight.settlement_expression: The district uses open vertical volume and long safety setbacks; inhabited quarters cluster behind fortified windbreaks rather than wrapping the machinery tightly.
Ghast / Magma / Froglight.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Froglights become prestigious lighting exports; magma cream feeds brewing; ghast drops support specialist crafting and transport-related demand.
Ghast / Magma / Froglight.player_build_guidance: Preserve dramatic void and height around the farms. The resource district should feel like it occupies dangerous airspace, not just floor area.

Hoglin.why_here: A stockade district on the ash coast gives hostile livestock production a distinct cultural expression separate from both surface animal husbandry and fortress mobs.
Hoglin.farm_architecture: Heavy stockades, feeding/handling alleys, protected slaughter/collection structures, smokehouse-style storage and fortified worker barracks.
Hoglin.settlement_expression: This is the most agricultural-looking Ember district, but all forms remain defensive, heat-resistant and compact.
trade_routes: portal cold-chain/provision route to Hearthlands and Transit
Hoglin.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Food output can supplement Hearthlands/Transit provisioning; animal-style outputs create a cultural contrast with Isles of Plenty husbandry.
Hoglin.player_build_guidance: Make the difference between Nether handling culture and tropical husbandry obvious: walls, gates, escape control and harsh materials dominate.

Nether Stoneworks.why_here: Nether-native block production belongs near the dimension's own quarry-fort culture while the Volcano remains the surface world's lava/basalt foundry civilization.
Nether Stoneworks.farm_architecture: Blackstone/basalt quarry-forts, block yards, lava-cut retaining works, crushing/crafting halls and heavy causeway depots.
Nether Stoneworks.settlement_expression: A low, massive district that reads as the geological foundation of Ember Coast rather than a copy of Stone Highlands.
imports: Timberlands specialty wood only where necessary
trade_routes: construction supply to Transit/Shrouded expedition infrastructure
Nether Stoneworks.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Surface basalt demand should be split intentionally: Volcano supplies its own caldera-derived identity; Ember supplies Nether-native stone traditions and variants.
Nether Stoneworks.player_build_guidance: Do not make this a generic quarry. Use fortress logistics, portal-era retaining works and blackstone causeways to distinguish it from Stone Highlands.

Enderman.why_here: End-adapted settlement and controlled portal access make Enderman production part of a secretive expedition economy rather than an ordinary mob farm.
Enderman.farm_architecture: Sparse Enderman courts, concealed drop/collection towers, long empty approach paths, observation chambers and isolated storage vaults.
Enderman.settlement_expression: Production occupies one distinct district of the hidden capital with large intentional voids separating it from habitation and shulker/storage areas.
imports: Ember blaze-derived progression inputs where needed
exports: End expedition supplies and access materials
trade_routes: controlled technical exchange with Crystal Deep
Enderman.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Ender pearls feed transport/progression systems and specialist crafting, with distribution intentionally controlled rather than open-market bulk handling.
Enderman.player_build_guidance: Use distance, silence and concealment as architecture. The farm should feel like a dangerous court the settlement learned to live beside.

Shulker & Storage.why_here: Shulker production naturally supports an End-derived storage culture, but its outputs become a strategic export rather than turning the region into the archipelago's general warehouse district.
Shulker & Storage.farm_architecture: Sealed shulker vault courts, vertical containment cells, shell-processing rooms and compact expedition depots with unusual geometry.
Shulker & Storage.settlement_expression: The district is denser and more enclosed than the Enderman court but remains physically separate from ordinary habitation.
local_processing: shulker-box crafting where inputs are imported
imports: Transit freight containers and expedition supplies
Shulker & Storage.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Shulker boxes transform logistics across every region, but Grand Exchange remains the system-wide storage/sorting culture; Shrouded Isles supplies the special container technology.
Shulker & Storage.player_build_guidance: Architecturally separate production from the storage-service economy it enables elsewhere. This region makes the container; it does not become the global warehouse.

Chorus & Purpur.why_here: A remote End-material enclave allows chorus cultivation and purpur processing to become landscape architecture rather than a surface-style crop farm.
Chorus & Purpur.farm_architecture: Chorus gardens, widely spaced cultivation courts, purpur terraces, narrow bridges and sparse processing pavilions.
Chorus & Purpur.settlement_expression: Cultivation is intentionally dispersed with long empty intervals; processing structures appear as isolated geometric compounds rather than dense industry.
Chorus & Purpur.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Purpur becomes a rare prestige material outside the End, reinforcing the idea that imported End architecture is expensive and selective.
Chorus & Purpur.player_build_guidance: Let empty space dominate. Chorus production should feel like an alien agricultural landscape, not rows hidden in a barn.

End Obsidian & Special Systems.why_here: End-specific renewable/special systems belong at the most remote experimental enclave where strange mechanics are culturally expected and access can be restricted.
End Obsidian & Special Systems.farm_architecture: Obsidian works, sealed experimental courts, portal-service structures, reinforced observation towers and isolated maintenance platforms.
End Obsidian & Special Systems.settlement_expression: The district is sparse and technical, with experimental compounds separated from chorus settlements by wilderness and long paths.
trade_routes: technical exchange with Engineer's Reach and Crystal Deep
End Obsidian & Special Systems.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Obsidian supports portal infrastructure and high-durability construction; rare special outputs stay on controlled routes rather than ordinary commodity flows.
End Obsidian & Special Systems.player_build_guidance: Treat experimental safety and remoteness as the settlement logic. Avoid making strange End mechanics visually ordinary.

cross_phase_resource_links.downstream: mobile storage without replacing Grand Exchange sorting

completion_note: Phase 2 completes the previously queued hostile, oceanic, transportation, Nether and End resource families. The next resource-planning layer is route-level physical logistics and island-by-island import/export dependency design.
